note: Marginal carbon intensity by hour, kg CO2 per MWh, shaped like a PJM summer weekday: coal on the margin overnight, solar pushing the midday hours down, inefficient gas peakers in the evening ramp. Illustrative, not measured.

scenarios.name: industrial batch
scenarios.title: Six-hour deferrable batch process
scenarios.description: A process that must run six hours somewhere in the day and does not care when.

scenarios.name: fleet charging
scenarios.title: Depot fleet charging inside an overnight window
scenarios.description: Vehicles are plugged in at 18:00 and must be full by 06:00, so only the evening peak and the overnight hours are available. The optimum here is worse than the day's best hours, which is the point: the window, not the algorithm, is what limits the saving.

scenarios.name: flat profile
scenarios.title: A day with no carbon signal
scenarios.description: When intensity barely moves, the optimal schedule saves almost nothing and the ratio bound collapses toward one. Worth having in the library: a scheduler that reports large savings on a day like this is reporting a bug.
